subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A sperm cell has many mitochondria. What is this an adaptation for?
options: Providing energy for the tail to swim to the egg
questions.explain: The many mitochondria release energy for the flagellum (tail) to swim to the egg.

questions.q: Which statement about light microscopes compared with electron microscopes is correct?
options: Light microscopes use beams of electrons to form an image
Light microscopes are cheaper and can view living specimens
Light microscopes have higher magnification and resolution
Light microscopes can show the inside detail of organelles clearly
questions.explain: Light microscopes are cheaper and can be used to look at living cells, but have lower magnification and resolution than electron microscopes.

questions.q: Which part of a bacterial cell can carry extra genes, for example genes for antibiotic resistance?
questions.explain: Plasmids are small rings of DNA, separate from the main chromosome, that can carry extra genes such as for antibiotic resistance.

questions.q: A root hair cell has a long projection. How does this help its function?
options: It allows the cell to photosynthesise
It helps the cell carry oxygen
It increases surface area for absorbing water and minerals
questions.explain: The long extension gives a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.

questions.q: What is the function of the cell wall in a plant cell?
options: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The plant cell wall is made of cellulose and provides strength and support.

questions.q: An image of a cell is 30 mm long and the magnification is ×1500. What is the actual size?
questions.explain: Actual = image ÷ magnification = 30 mm ÷ 1500 = 0.02 mm = 20 µm.

questions.q: To convert a measurement in millimetres (mm) into micrometres (µm), you should:
questions.explain: There are 1000 micrometres in a millimetre, so you multiply mm by 1000 to get µm.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the levels of organisation, smallest to largest?
questions.explain: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make organ systems.

questions.q: A cell is 0.05 mm wide. What is this in micrometres (µm)?
Which feature is present in a bacterial (prokaryotic) cell?
options: A single loop of DNA in the cytoplasm
questions.explain: Bacteria have no nucleus; their genetic material is a single circular DNA loop free in the cytoplasm, sometimes with plasmids.

questions.q: A xylem vessel cell is hollow and has no living contents and no end walls. This adapts it to:
questions.explain: Hollow, dead xylem cells joined end to end form continuous tubes for water transport.

questions.q: A cell appears 40 mm wide under a microscope at a magnification of ×400. What is its actual width?
questions.explain: Actual size = image size ÷ magnification = 40 ÷ 400 = 0.1 mm.

questions.q: What is the function of ribosomes?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.q: Which of these is the smallest and would need the highest magnification to be seen?
questions.explain: A mitochondrion is a sub-cellular organelle and is smaller than a whole bacterium or animal cell.

questions.q: What is the main function of the nucleus in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Controlling the cell and storing genetic material
Controlling what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the DNA and controls the cell's activities.

questions.q: Why does an electron microscope allow us to see more detail than a light microscope?
options: It only works on living cells
It has a much higher magnification and resolution
It uses a brighter light source
It magnifies but has lower resolution
questions.explain: Electron microscopes have far higher magnification and resolution, revealing sub-cellular structures.

questions.q: A group of similar cells working together to carry out a particular function is called a:
questions.explain: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.

questions.q: In which organelle does most aerobic respiration take place?
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the correct order from a single cell up to a whole organism?
options: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
questions.explain: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and these make up the organism.

questions.q: The magnification equation is:
questions.explain: Magnification = image size ÷ actual size.

questions.q: What is the role of the permanent vacuole in a plant cell?
options: Contains cell sap to keep the cell turgid (firm)
questions.explain: The vacuole is filled with cell sap and helps keep the plant cell rigid and supported.

questions.q: A muscle cell contains a large number of mitochondria. This is an adaptation to:
options: Release plenty of energy for contraction
questions.explain: Muscle cells need lots of energy to contract, so they have many mitochondria for aerobic respiration.
